quizzes.stem: A team has 40,000 classification requests, none needed before tomorrow, on Claude Sonnet 5.5. Which plan should they choose?

options.a: Send them as a batch with `stream: true`, so results arrive as they finish
options.b: Send them as a batch at the standard price, since a batch only helps throughput
options.c: Send them one by one, since a batch cannot take more than a few hundred
options.d: Send them as one batch at half the price, since a wait of hours costs nothing

explanation.d: The page says "All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices" and that the batch suits work where "Immediate responses are not required".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the discount covers "input, output and special tokens" at half price.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A Message Batch is limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size", which is far above a few hundred.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Batch results come back as a single file, not a stream."

quizzes.stem: A batch request body copied from a live endpoint contains `speed` set to fast. What is the outcome for that request?

options.a: A validation error comes back, since that parameter is unsupported here
options.b: The batch runs at the fast rate, since the parameter is passed through unchanged
options.c: The parameter is dropped silently, and the batch runs at the standard rate
options.d: The batch is accepted, but the fast rate is billed in place of the discount

explanation.a: The page says these parameters are "refused with a validation error".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Fast mode tunes synchronous latency, which doesn't apply to asynchronous batch processing."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says they are "refused with a validation error", not dropped.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices", with no fast rate in a batch.

quizzes.stem: A job has 250,000 small requests. How must it be submitted?

options.a: In two batches, since each holds up to 128,000 requests
options.b: In one batch, since the size limit is counted in bytes and not in requests
options.c: In at least three parts, since one batch holds 100,000 items at most
options.d: In one batch, and the system splits it into parts by itself

explanation.c: The page says "A Message Batch is limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size, whichever is reached first", so 250,000 needs three.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "whichever is reached first" means the request count limit applies as well as the size.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the stated limit is "either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB", not 128,000.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the system does not split an oversize job, since "A batch above 256 MB returns a 413 `request_too_large` error.", and "The practice at the end of the next page does the cutting."

quizzes.stem: The first line of a result file belongs to the request sent third. What should the program do?

options.a: Treat the file as corrupt, since entries must follow the order of submission
options.b: Match each entry by its `custom_id`, since the order carries no meaning
options.c: Sort by finishing time, since that is the order that counts for the match
options.d: Match by position once the first entries are read, since the rest follow suit

explanation.b: The page says "always use the `custom_id` field" to match, since the file order carries no meaning.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the file "may not match the ordering of requests when the batch was created".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "The result lines carry `custom_id` and a `result` whose `type` is one of the four.", with no finishing time to sort by, and "Position in the file means nothing."
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Batch results can be returned in any order".

quizzes.stem: A batch ends with 900 succeeded results, 50 errored, 30 canceled and 20 expired. Which results are billed?

options.a: The 900 and the 20 that timed out, as those had reached a queue
options.b: The 900 and the 50 that failed on an error, as both ran a model
options.c: All 1,000, as the discount is a flat half of the total
options.d: The 900 that worked, as the other three kinds carry no charge

explanation.d: The page says "You will not be billed for these requests." of the three failure types.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "You will not be billed for these requests." is stated for the errored results too.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Only the `succeeded` results carry tokens that are billed."
explanation.a: Ruled out because an expired request means "the 24 hours passed before this request was sent", so it never ran.

quizzes.stem: A result line for one request shows an error of type invalid_request_error. What is the sound next step?

options.a: Resubmit it unchanged, since a failure is usually a one-off
options.b: Rework the body for a new batch, since its content is at fault
options.c: Wait for the same batch to retry it, since that is automatic
options.d: Drop it, since an errored entry cannot join a new batch

explanation.b: The page's table says for this error "fix it first; the same request fails again", and then a new batch can carry it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because of "fix it first; the same request fails again".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "once a batch has been submitted, it cannot be modified", so a batch does not retry on its own.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "Collect the failures into a new, smaller batch."

quizzes.stem: A nightly job of 80,000 requests comes to 300 MB, and the answers are wanted by the next evening. Which plan should the team follow?

options.a: Send one batch and read the results in the order they were sent
options.b: Split into at least two batches and match each result by its id
options.c: Split into batches that first pre-warm the cache with `max_tokens: 0`
options.d: Send one batch with `speed` fast to finish before the next evening

explanation.b: The page says "A Message Batch is limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size, whichever is reached first", so 300 MB needs two batches although 80,000 is under the count, and the ids match the results.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A batch above 256 MB returns a 413 `request_too_large` error.", and "Batch results can be returned in any order".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page 1 table says "pre-warming a cache is not supported" in a batch, so `max_tokens: 0` is refused.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page 1 table marks `speed` as refused, and "Fast mode tunes synchronous latency" does not apply in a batch.

quizzes.stem: A team tries to download its output 35 days after the job was created. What do they find?

options.a: The batch still shows up, but its results lapsed almost a week earlier
options.b: The downloads are fine, since the 29 days count from the end of processing
options.c: The record is deleted, since it expires together with its downloads
options.d: The downloads are fine, since each read of the batch renews the window

explanation.a: "Results live for 29 days after `created_at`", so on day 35 the results lapsed six days earlier, while "you may still view the Batch" after the window.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Results live for 29 days after `created_at`", not after the end.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "you may still view the Batch" after the window.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Batch results are available for 29 days after creation.", a fixed count that no read of the batch renews.

quizzes.stem: A batch of 3,000 requests ends with 2,700 succeeded and 300 expired. What is the sound handling?

options.a: Resend the 300 unchanged, since they never got to run
options.b: Resubmit all 3,000 so the results come from one run
options.c: Drop the 300, since an expired request cannot be sent again
options.d: Fix the 300 first, since an expired request is an invalid one

explanation.a: The page's table says an expired request is resubmitted unchanged, and the finished answers stay.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "Collect the failures into a new, smaller batch.", so only the 300 go in again.
explanation.c: Ruled out because an expired request means "the 24 hours passed before this request was sent", so it can go in again.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the batch ran out of time first" is the cause of an expiry, not a bad request.

quizzes.stem: A program prices the succeeded tokens of a Claude Sonnet 5.5 batch at $2 and $10 per million, and the total exceeds the invoice. What is the likely cause?

options.a: It counts entries past the spend limit, which the invoice leaves out
options.b: It counts retried requests twice, since each retry adds a line
options.c: It uses the standard rates, where this route charges only half
options.d: It counts polling calls, since each poll is billed as a request

explanation.c: Page 1 gives "At the standard $2 and $10" for Claude Sonnet 5.5, and "All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices.", so the batch rates are $1 and $5.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "every request has exactly one result" once processing has ended.
explanation.a: Ruled out because page 1 says "The limit is not a hard stop for a batch.", so entries past it are still billed.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Poll the batch by its `id`, with a wait between polls." returns a status and no message, so no tokens.
